messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Migration, Physical fitness and exercise, Specific diseases, disorders and medical conditions, Government, political systems and organisations, Political behaviour and attitudes, Social welfare policy, Specific social services: use and availability, and Employment in Germany during the 2020s, matching this research need: Longitudinal German panel data on individual attitudes and preferences relevant to political and economic decision-making, collected online from the general population.
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: German Internet Panel GIP longitudinal online general population attitudes preferences political economic decision making dataset
GESIS German Internet Panel data 2020 2024 waves DOI
German online panel longitudinal attitudes migration health employment politics 2020 dataset
action.query: German Internet Panel GIP longitudinal online general population attitudes preferences political economic decision making dataset

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"German Internet Panel (GIP) – Longitudinal Online Panel, 2012–2026","url_or_doi":"https://paneldata.org/gip/","justification":"Excellent match. The German Internet Panel (GIP), conducted by the University of Mannheim, is specifically designed to collect longitudinal data on individual attitudes and preferences relevant to political and economic decision-making. It uses probability-based sampling of Germany's general population, with online questionnaires administered approximately every two months. Data collected during the 2020s cover migration, health, physical activity, political institutions, political attitudes, welfare policies, social inequality, employment, and demographic characteristics. Individual respondents can be followed across multiple waves, making this particularly suitable for studying changes in preferences and attitudes over time."},{"title":"German Internet Panel (GIP) – Official Study and Data Access Portal","url_or_doi":"https://www.uni-mannheim.de/en/gip/","justification":"Official University of Mannheim landing page for the German Internet Panel. The study surveys thousands of participants across Germany online and investigates political and economic preferences, attitudes toward government reforms, welfare state policies, health, employment, and social issues. Its longitudinal design supports within-person analyses of changing political and economic attitudes throughout the 2020s. Scientific Use Files are distributed through the GESIS Data Archive, subject to data access requirements."},{"title":"German Internet Panel, Wave 70 (March 2024)","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA9052","justification":"Highly relevant individual wave of the German Internet Panel, collected in March 2024 from 3,681 respondents. The dataset includes migration, political attitudes, social inequality, minorities, religion, values, and social attitudes. Respondents belong to the longitudinal GIP sample, allowing this wave to be linked with other survey waves for analysis of changes in attitudes and preferences. Data were collected through web-based self-administered questionnaires using probability-based sampling. DOI: 10.4232/1.14744."},{"title":"German Internet Panel, Wave 74 (November 2024)","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.cessda.eu/detail/b69725743af742fc76fd17a59cf1cf77f51c71386659da53a868f1e0e8268fdc?lang=en","justification":"Strong match for research on employment, economic preferences, political behavior, and social policy attitudes in Germany. This November 2024 GIP wave includes employment status, occupational position, remote working arrangements, employment contracts, public-sector employment, life satisfaction, political party preferences, and attitudes toward income redistribution. The online survey forms part of a continuing longitudinal panel of Germany's general population and supports analysis of political and economic attitudes across repeated observations."},{"title":"German Internet Panel, Wave 76 (March 2025)","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA9211","justification":"Relevant recent GIP wave focusing on elections, government, political systems, political organizations, and political behavior and attitudes. Collected online in March 2025, the dataset contains responses from 3,463 individuals. It uses the GIP's longitudinal probability-based sample of people recruited from Germany's general population. Particularly appropriate for examining political preferences, electoral attitudes, and changes in political decision-making over time when combined with earlier GIP waves."},{"title":"DeZIM.panel – German Longitudinal Online Access Panel on Migration, Integration, and Social Attitudes","url_or_doi":"https://www.dezim-institut.de/en/dezimfdz/online-access-panel/","justification":"Very strong complementary dataset for longitudinal research on migration, political attitudes, health, employment, and social welfare in Germany during the 2020s. Established in 2021, the DeZIM.panel follows individuals with and without migration backgrounds through repeated surveys. Approximately 7,000 participants initially agreed to longitudinal participation. Topics include political attitudes and values, health and subjective well-being, employment, education, migration, integration, and social experiences. The panel supports analysis of changes in individual attitudes and experiences, although its emphasis on migration makes it more specialized than the German Internet Panel."},{"title":"DeZIM.panel – Longitudinal Scientific Use File, Recruitment Survey and Follow-up Waves","url_or_doi":"https://www.dezim-institut.de/en/news/new-dezimpanel-dataset-extensive-longitudinal-data-on-migration-and-integration-available-for-research/","justification":"Relevant longitudinal dataset covering German population attitudes and experiences during the 2020s. The Scientific Use File announced in June 2024 contains the 2021 recruitment survey, an initial rapid survey, and eight regular follow-up waves. It enables individual-level analysis of political attitudes, social issues, migration experiences, integration, health, and economic circumstances over time. The repeated-measures structure is particularly useful for examining relationships between migration backgrounds, political preferences, and perceptions of social and economic conditions."},{"title":"GESIS Panel – Longitudinal General Population Survey in Germany","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gesis-panel","justification":"Strong alternative for longitudinal research on social, political, and economic attitudes among Germany's general population. The GESIS Panel.pop Population Sample uses probability-based recruitment of the adult German-speaking population and collects repeated survey responses through online and paper questionnaires. It provides longitudinal data on attitudes, social conditions, health-related topics, and other social science research questions. Its mixed-mode design makes it slightly less specific to the requirement for exclusively online collection, but it is valuable for studying changes in individual preferences and attitudes during the 2020s. Cross-sectional and longitudinal survey datasets are available for secondary analysis."}]}
